scene.batteryArrangement: four batteries directly on the floor in a 2 × 2 footprint
scene.classTFuseMounting: two holders mount directly to the plywood wall above the floor battery bank; no separate backplate
scene.heavyBatteryCableRoute: terminal-derived rectilinear lead-outs around the floor battery footprint, selected together with the balancer leads by a cable-clearance solver
scene.junctionCableEntries: 33 service circuits comprise 35 optimized terminal-to-terminal wire segments through 14 cable glands plus one Starlink bulkhead DC jack, arranged by the optimizer in two rows on the bottom face. The 100 A MPPT breaker and six service breakers are resettable; only the two battery Class T devices and Victron-specified small inline fuses remain non-resettable. The SmartShunt's supplied 1 A fused Vbatt+ lead occupies the seventh positive-bus connection. UniFi, USB and both light runs each arrive as one positive/negative pair through one gland and split only inside the box
scene.junctionMounting: back of enclosure flush to plywood with zero cable routes behind it; every external DC, data and service connection exits through the bottom face, while the three-rocker control frame passes through the otherwise unused fixed left sidewall
scene.layoutSolver: The offline layout solver independently generates device envelopes, port coordinates and major cable centerlines from a saved evolutionary placement before Three.js rendering; its collision-aware bundle keeps direct battery runs in low wall-adjacent corridors, while a separate seeded evolutionary junction optimizer evolves the internal component positions, arbitrary two-row bottom-gland order and wire-routing order
scene.ceilingCableRouting: One thin white two-conductor Starlink OEM cable leaves the junction bulkhead jack and turns directly toward the Mini; it is not abstracted into separate rooftop red/black runs. Two identical five-inch utility lights each use one positive and one negative conductor from source-side switching; the indoor unit is suspended with its lens down, while the exterior unit is wall-mounted. Starlink Ethernet descends on the Starlink side and travels directly left to UniFi without the former rightward overshoot.
scene.cameraControls: ofxGrabCam-inspired perspective camera: ray-pick the XYZ surface point under mouse or touch, use upright world-Y yaw and pitch around that off-axis point with roll locked out, and scale zoom/pan at its depth; one touch orbits and two touches pan plus pinch-zoom
scene.cableGeometry: one continuous tube surface per route with tangent corner-contained bends, seamless adjacent corners, tangent render handoffs and stable greedy board-depth lanes

assumptions: The back wall, wall board, panel rack, generator and small protection-enclosure dimensions are planning envelopes, not surveyed site measurements. Side walls and roof planes are omitted from the review model.
The array is shown close to the north side of the building. The two 4 mm² PV pairs retain a conservative 15 m one-way design allowance even though the illustrated route is shorter.

Both PV strings retain independent positive and negative home-run conductors all the way to one indoor entry enclosure. For this two-string array, the other string can contribute only about one module Isc (14.20 A) into a faulted string, below the Suntech module's 25 A maximum series-fuse rating; the base design therefore omits the separate outdoor fuse/combiner. The indoor enclosure still provides protected parallel terminals, a two-pole 40 A DC disconnect and Type 2 SPD. Final cable ampacity and local-code review remain mandatory.
The array faces north at an 18° planning tilt, consistent with Fiji's latitude and government residential-solar guidance; final angle and shading require site verification.
Small conductors are slightly widened so individual polarity, protected positives, unswitched negative returns and data paths remain visible.

Ordinary power conductors begin approximately 35 mm in front of the plywood and receive stable wall lanes. Flush-junction bypasses briefly stand farther forward—up to about 245 mm from plywood—to clear the enclosure face before returning toward their terminal; no route occupies the inaccessible space behind the box.

All battery shelving is omitted. Four batteries sit directly on the floor in two side-by-side series strings, arranged as a 2 × 2 footprint. The two Class T holders mount directly to the plywood and heavy conductors route around the battery footprint.

The four main battery leads and six battery-balancer leads are routed as one ordered terminal-derived bundle. Candidate terminal lead-outs, bend orders and depth lanes are accepted only after a three-dimensional cable-to-cable audit, including parallel overlaps and endpoint-to-interior contacts. The modeled harness retains at least 3 mm surface clearance except where conductors intentionally share a battery terminal.

Every gland crossing uses one continuous centerline from its internal termination through the enclosure wall into the outgoing run. The Starlink exception is intentionally connectorized: separate internal red/black wires terminate on a two-pin bulkhead jack, and one white OEM cable begins outside it.

The 86.4 × 58.4 mm three-position switch frame is shown through the fixed enclosure sidewall. INTERNET is DPST, independently switching the separately breakered 24 V Starlink and UniFi positives; INSIDE and OUTSIDE are SPST source-side light controls. Every load negative bypasses the rockers. A separate small black return serves only the embedded indicator LEDs.

Every green conductor terminates at a modeled stud: the electrode and array frame share the electrode connection, and dedicated studs on a visible main PE bar feed PV protection, SmartSolar chassis, MultiPlus chassis, AC output protection and Ekrano GX. Protective earth is not tied to the DC-negative bus in this planning model.

The SmartShunt's supplied fused Vbatt+ lead is routed from the protected positive bus to its voltage-sense terminal. Its single Aux input is reserved rather than presented as whole-bank midpoint monitoring because one input cannot independently supervise both parallel 24 V strings.

The supplied MultiPlus battery-temperature sensor runs to Battery 1's negative terminal. Ekrano DVCC uses SmartShunt voltage/current for Shared Voltage Sense and Shared Current Sense and the MultiPlus sensor for Shared Temperature Sense, so no separate Smart Battery Sense is included.

Each battery balancer has an independent two-conductor dry-contact alarm cable to one Ekrano digital input; the two units remain necessary because the two series strings must be balanced and diagnosed independently.

Each complete cable route renders as one continuous tube surface rather than separate open cylinders and bend pieces. This removes polygon-ring gaps when two bends are close together. Bends use tangent, corner-contained quadratic geometry; each curve stays within the intended turn and cannot curl backwards in perspective. A greedy minimum-conflict planner gives each complete board route one stable depth lane; ceiling departures retain that lane instead of snapping back to a shared wall datum. The geometry audit checks both reverse bends and non-terminal crossings.

Camera interactions ray-pick the visible XYZ point beneath the mouse or touch centroid. Upright orbit and zoom preserve that off-axis point's screen position; roll is locked to world-up and pan scale derives from picked depth. One finger orbits, two fingers pan and pinch-zoom, and empty-space interactions reuse the last valid projected depth, following the ofxGrabCam interaction model.

The junction result is generated by scripts/optimize-junction-layout.ts with a deterministic seed and a default 600-second time budget. It warm-starts from the saved result unless --fresh is specified, evolves all internal component centers, both bottom-face gland rows and route order, checkpoints atomically, and saves the complete genome, convergence history, metrics and renderer-ready routes in data/junction-optimized-layout.json. Routing depth is measured forward from the inner back panel. Every conductor begins on a common 60 mm service plane; radius-aware bridge intervals are merged across the whole rectilinear polyline, may move toward or away from the back panel, and account for each bottom gland row's physical depth. A reserved bottom gutter keeps ordinary cross-box runs away from gland breakouts.
Gland positions and bend radii remain a planning layout and require a full-size mock-up with the actual parts before drilling or ordering preterminated cables.

24 V UniFi protected + in / switched + out
